|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241203052535/https://www.firstpost.com/india/drdo-to-make-4-variants-of-nasm-mr-missile-will-boost-indian-navy-against-china-11964702.html |archive-date=2024-12-03 |access-date=2024-09-03 |website=Firstpost |language=en-us}}{{Cite web |title=DRDO To Make 4 Variants of NASM-MR Missile, Will Boost Indian Navy Against China |url=https://www.indiandefensenews.in/2023/01/drdo-to-make-4-variants-of-nasm-mr.html#goog_rewarded |access-date=2024-09-03|date=2023-01-11|website=indiandefensenews.in}} The NASM-MR will belong to the same class as the U.S.-origin [[Harpoon (missile)|Harpoon missile]].{{Cite web |last=Mandal |first=Sohini |date=2026-06-15 |title=India conducts maiden flight test of NASM-MR anti-ship missile |url=https://www.janes.com/defence-intelligence-insights/defence-news/defence/india-conducts-maiden-flight-test-of-nasm-mr-anti-ship-missile |access-date=2026-07-13 |website=janes.com |language=en}} ==Development== On 6 November 2023, the DRDO completed the preliminary design review of the NASM-MR missile and was proceeding for developing [[wind tunnel]] model for testing the to finalize the aerodynamic configuration.{{Cite tweet |number=1721393222612914381 |user=Varun55484761 |title=Preliminary Design Review of DRDO Naval Anti-Ship Missile–Medium Range(NASM-MR) completed... |first=Varun |last=Karthikeyan |date=2023-11-06 |access-date=2024-09-03}} On 30 November 2023, Defence Acquisition Council (DAC), chaired by the [[Minister of Defence (India)|Defence Minister]], [[Rajnath Singh]], under the [[Ministry of Defence (India)|Ministry of Defence]], cleared the acquisition of the Medium Range Anti-Ship Missiles (MRAShM) for [[Surface combatant|surface warships]] of the Indian Navy which is envisaged as a lightweight Surface-to-Surface Missile to be used as a primary offensive weapon onboard Indian Naval Ships.{{Cite web |date=2023-11-30 |title=Defence Acquisition Council approves capital acquisition proposals worth Rs 2.23 lakh crore to enhance the operational capabilities of the Armed Forces |url=https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1981135 |access-date=2024-09-03 |website=Press Information Bureau}} An acquisition of 450 examples are expected.{{Cite web |last=Menon |first=Adithya Krishna |date=2026-06-16 |title=India Conducts Spate of Tests for Anti-Ship, Land Attack, BMD And Hypersonic Ground Attack Missiles |url=https://www.navalnews.com/naval-news/2026/06/india-conducts-spate-of-tests-for-anti-ship-land-attack-bmd-and-hypersonic-ground-attack-missiles/ |access-date=2026-06-25 |website=Naval News |language=en-US}} The integration of NASM-MR with [[MiG-29K]] was completed in 2023. The fighter jet's and the missile's electrical and mechanical interfaces have been checked. In order to verify missile's target and guidance package under actual flight conditions, live-fire tests will be conducted after carry and separation trials. According to mission requirements, the missile can follow specified [[Waypoint|waypoints]] and have the ability to [[Sea skimming|sea skim]].{{Cite web |date=10 October 2025 |title=2023-24 Annual Report |url=https://mod.gov.in/sites/default/files/AR_2023-24-new-23-9-2025.pdf |access-date=10 October 2025 |website=Ministry of Defence, Government of India}}{{Cite web |last=Pillai |first=Joy |date=2025-10-12 |title=Big tension for China, Pakistan as India successfully integrates NASM-MR missile into…, ahead of… |url=https://www.india.com/news/india/big-tension-for-china-pakistan-as-india-successfully-integrates-nasm-mr-missile-into-mig-29k-ahead-of-trials-indian-navy-indian-army-8128156/ |access-date=2025-10-13 |website=india.com |language=en}} With the integration of the missile with MiG-29K completed, the maiden flight tests of the weapon is scheduled in the first quarter of 2026.{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2026-01-11 |title=MiG-29K Successfully Integrates Indigenous NASM-MR Missile in Indian Navy |url=https://defence.newsd.in/military/navy/mig-29k-successfully-integrates-indigenous-nasm-mr-missile-in-indian-navy |access-date=2026-01-13 |website=Newsd Defence |language=en-US}} During the June 2026 trials, the missile was equipped with a [[Bunker buster|penetration-cum-blast]] warhead, an engine source from [[Safran]], and a [[solid propellant]] [[Booster (rocketry)|booster]] which is unique for the ground-launched variant. However, for long-term production variants, the missile will utilise an indigenous [[Gas Turbine Research Establishment#Advanced Turbo Gas Generator|Advanced Turbo Gas Generator]] (ATGG) [[Spool (aeronautics)|single-spool]] compact [[turbojet]] developed by [[Gas Turbine Research Establishment]] and Azad Engineering Limited.{{Cite news |last= |first= |date=2024-05-23 |title=Azad Engineering bags contract for advanced turbo gas generator engine from DRDO lab GTRE |url=https://www.thehindu.com/business/azad-engineering-bags-contract-for-advanced-turbo-gas-generator-engine-from-drdo-lab-gtre/article68208249.ece |access-date=2026-07-05 |work=The Hindu |language=en-IN |issn=0971-751X}}{{Cite web |last=Rastogi |first=Manav |date=2024-12-27 |title=Indigenous ATGG Engine by Azad Engineering to Power India's Medium-Range Anti-Ship Missile Program |url=https://defence.in/threads/indigenous-atgg-engine-by-azad-engineering-to-power-indias-medium-range-anti-ship-missile-program.12041/ |access-date=2026-07-05 |website=Defence News India |language=en-US}} The ground-launched variant can also be offered as a product. The first ATGG indigenous expendable turbojet engine with a thrust class of {{Convert|350|kgf|kN|abbr=on}} was delivered on 22 July 2026.{{Cite press release |title=Successful development of first indigenous Expendable Turbo Jet Engine of 350 kg thrust class |date=2026-07-23 |publisher=[[Press Information Bureau]] |url=https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2288576®=48&lang=1 |access-date=2026-07-24}} == Trials == The first flight trial of the NASM-MR was conducted between 10 and 11 June 2026 from the [[Integrated Test Range]] (ITR).{{Cite web |last=Gupta |first=Shishir |date=2026-06-12 |title=India joins elite club with successful ballistic missile defence, anti-ship missile trials |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/india-joins-elite-club-with-successful-ballistic-missile-defence-anti-ship-missile-trials-101781278990240.html |access-date=2026-06-12 |website=Hindustan Times |language=en}} The missile was launched from a ground-based launcher.{{Cite press release |title=DRDO demonstrates the nation’s next-gen defence capabilities |date=2026-06-13 |publisher=[[Press Information Bureau]] |url=https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2272374®=48&lang=2 |access-date=2026-06-13}} ==Variants== There will be multiple variants of the missile will be developed. The variants include:{{Cite web |last= |date=2023-01-11 |title=DRDO to Make Four Variants of NASM-MR Missile |url=https://raksha-anirveda.com/drdo-to-make-four-variants-of-nasm-mr-missile/ |access-date=2026-06-24 |website=raksha-anirveda.com |language=en}} * '''Air-launched variant''': Will be deployed onboard [[Fixed-wing aircraft|fixed-wing]] [[fighter aircraft]] like the [[MiG-29K]] and [[maritime patrol aircraft]] (MPA) like [[Boeing P-8 Poseidon|Boeing P-8I Neptune]]. An [[HAL Tejas Mk1A]] can carry five NASM-MR missiles. '''Range''': {{Convert|290|km}}. * '''Ship-launched variant''': Being developed under the Medium Range Anti-Ship Missiles (MRAShM) programme for deployment from [[Vertical launching system|vertical launchers]] aboard frontline warships. It will include an additional [[Solid-propellant rocket|solid-fuel rocket]] booster. '''Range''': {{Convert|350|km}}. * '''Submarine-launched variant''': Will include an additional [[Solid-propellant rocket|solid-fuel rocket]] booster. '''Range''': >{{Convert|100|km}}. * '''Coastal defence batteries''': May take longer than the other three variants due to Indian Navy requirements. ==See also== {{Portal|India|Rocketry}} * {{anl|NASM-SR}} * {{lwc|Harpoon (missile)|Harpoon}} * {{lwc|Exocet}} * {{lwc|Kalibr (missile family)|Kalibr}} * {{lwc|Kh-35}} * {{lwc|Naval Strike Missile}} * {{lwc|Type 12}} – (Japan) * {{lwc|Type 88}} – (Japan) == References == {{reflist}} {{Defence Research and Development Organisation|NASM-MR}} [[Category:Anti-ship cruise missiles of India]] [[Category:Anti-ship missiles of India]] {{missile-stub}}
extract: Naval Anti-Ship Missile–Medium Range (NASM–MR) or Medium Range Anti-Ship Missiles (MRAShM) is an all-weather, over-the-horizon anti-ship missile being developed by the Defence Research and Development Organisation for the Indian Navy for use against small to medium sized warships like frigates, corvettes, and destroyers. The NASM-MR will belong to the same class as the U.S.-origin Harpoon missile.
